report:
### Conclusion
Yes, scientific evidence indicates that olive leaf extract (OLE) can help lower high blood pressure, particularly in individuals with prehypertension or stage-1 hypertension.

### Key Evidence & Mechanisms
* **Clinical Efficacy:** Systematic reviews and randomized controlled trials show that OLE supplementation significantly reduces both systolic and diastolic blood pressure. In a landmark active-controlled trial, taking 500 mg of OLE twice daily was as effective at lowering blood pressure in stage-1 hypertensive patients as standard doses of Captopril (an ACE inhibitor), while also improving lipid levels.
* **Active Bioactive Compounds:** The antihypertensive properties of OLE are largely driven by polyphenols, primarily **oleuropein**. Oleuropein promotes vascular relaxation, exerts antioxidant effects, and inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE).
* **Dosage & Considerations:** Effective doses studied in clinical trials range from 500 mg to 1,000 mg daily. While generally safe, OLE may interact with prescription antihypertensives to cause abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension). Anyone considering OLE should consult a healthcare professional first.

### Sources

* Springer (Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis): https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13098-022-00920-y
* Phytotherapy Research (Meta-Analysis): https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ptr.8509
* Natural Health Research Institute (Mechanism Overview): https://naturalhealthresearch.org/olive-leaf-lowers-blood-pressure/
